This checklist is designed to drive the decisions that shape what the connector does before it is built - not to evaluate something already installed. Complete Sections 3 and 4 first. 1
What Claude Can See and Do in Salesforce
Typical Salesforce MCP connector capabilities - applies to any connector built or sourced
A Salesforce connector operates via the Salesforce REST API using OAuth credentials. Whatever the authenticated user (or integration user) can do in Salesforce, Claude can do. The table below covers the standard operation types any Salesforce connector exposes. The decisions in Section 4 determine which of these are enabled for School Tech.
Standard Salesforce Connector Capabilities
Operation What it means Risk level
search / SOQL queryRun structured queries across any object: Cases, Accounts, Contacts, Opps, KA, custom objects. Returns full field data.High - can surface any record the auth user can see
get_recordRead a specific record in full - all fields the authenticated user can see. Case details, Account fields, Opp amounts, etc.High - financial data, pipeline data, customer PII all visible
update_recordModify field values on existing records. Can update Cases, Accounts, Opportunities, Contacts, KA, and any custom object.Critical - direct writes to production records; no undo
create_recordCreate new records: new Cases, new Contacts, new Tasks, new log entries. Knowledge Articles are excluded by standing rule, drafts included - see section 6.High - creates persistent records in production org
delete_recordPermanently delete a record from Salesforce (goes to Recycle Bin, then purged).Critical - destructive; do not enable in V1
describe_objectRead the schema of a Salesforce object - field names, types, relationships. Used for admin help and audit tasks.Low - metadata only, no record data
run_reportExecute a saved Salesforce report and return results. Used for auditing, pipeline review, support metrics.Medium - read-only but returns aggregated sensitive data
get_flow / read flow metadataRead the definition and logic of a Salesforce Flow. Used for admin help, debugging, and flow documentation.Medium - exposes business logic; read-only is acceptable
deploy / update flowModify or deploy a Salesforce Flow directly in the org. Changes automation logic in production.Critical - broken flows can break business processes; do not enable
read security / permission setsRead user permission sets, profiles, sharing rules, and field-level security settings. Used for security audits.High - reveals your entire security model; read-only is acceptable for audit use
The most important thing to know: NEITHER connector has a platform gate. Gmail's send_message, reply and forward execute the moment they are called - there is no draft-only mode and no confirmation prompt (see the Google Access Security Checklist, corrected 2026-08-20). Salesforce is the same. In both cases the only control is a written prohibition in the project's instructions.md that names the tools. Do not calibrate Salesforce risk against a Gmail gate that does not exist. If you give Claude write access and allow direct execution, it will update records immediately with no review step. You must build the "propose before execute" model into the connector or the instructions - it does not happen automatically.

Data Risk Map - What's in Your Salesforce Org
School Tech specific - know what the AI will encounter before you connect
Object / Data TypeWhat it containsRisk LevelV1 Access Decision
Opportunities
Pipeline, deal values, close dates, sales stage, ARR		 Revenue forecasts, contract values, competitive deal details Critical Read-only. No write access in V1. Pipeline data is the most confidential business data in the org. Claude can read it to answer questions but should never update amounts, stages, or close dates without explicit confirmation.
Invoices / Subscription records
Invoice numbers, subscription terms, billing amounts		 Contract financial terms, renewal amounts, billing history Critical Read-only. Financial record updates must never be AI-executed without human review. Claude can look up an invoice number or subscription status; it should not modify billing records.
Security configuration
Permission sets, profiles, sharing rules, FLS settings		 Your entire org security model - who can see what Critical Read-only for audit assistance. Claude can read your security config to help diagnose permission issues. It must never modify permission sets, profiles, or sharing rules directly.
Cases
Support case records, case comments, status, priority, resolution notes		 Customer issues, internal notes, resolution history. No student data confirmed. High Read + propose updates. Claude can read cases and draft updates, but updates should be confirmed by the user before executing. Case comments can be created directly (lower risk than field updates).
Accounts (Districts)
District name, address, account type, products, contract status, owner		 Customer business profile. Core org record. No student data. High Read freely. Write with confirmation only. Account records are load-bearing - a bad field update (wrong account type, wrong owner, wrong status) can cascade through cases, reports, and automations.
Flows
Flow logic, triggers, actions, decision trees		 Business process automation - how records change, what emails fire, what happens on create/update High Read-only for help and audit. Claude can read flow logic to explain it, identify bugs, and suggest fixes. Never allow Claude to deploy or modify a flow directly. Propose-only: Claude writes the fix, a human deploys it.
Knowledge Articles
Published KA content, draft KAs, categories, review status		 Product help content, troubleshooting guides, internal reference articles Medium Read only. Article content is produced as HTML in chat and pasted in by a human. No API or CLI write, draft or published.
Contacts
District staff names, emails, phone numbers, titles, roles		 Customer PII - names, emails, direct phone numbers. Business contacts only, no students. Medium Read freely. Create and update with caution - duplicate contacts and bad data are common Salesforce problems. Claude should check for existing records before creating new Contacts.
Tasks / Activity log
Logged calls, emails, meeting notes attached to records		 History of customer interactions - what was said, when, by whom Medium Read freely. Creating tasks (logging activity) is safe and a good use case. Task creation does not require confirmation - it is additive and does not modify existing records.
Reports and Dashboards
Saved reports on pipeline, support volume, renewal tracking		 Aggregated business data - KPIs, counts, summaries. May include revenue figures. Medium Read-only. Running reports for auditing and admin help is a good use case. Claude should not modify or delete reports and dashboards.
No student data in Salesforce. Unlike Gmail (where district support emails may contain student records), School Tech's Salesforce org contains no student-level data. This removes the FERPA/Critical risk tier that applies to the Gmail integration and lowers the overall risk ceiling for this integration. The primary data risks here are financial (Opp/Invoice data) and business-confidential (pipeline, security config).
3
The Critical Decision: Propose vs. Execute
This single decision shapes the risk profile of the entire integration
Decide First
This is the Salesforce equivalent of the written send-prohibition on Gmail-connected projects - and neither one is enforced by the platform. You have to build both in. The decision you make here applies to every write operation Claude performs in Salesforce.
Core Decision
When Claude wants to update a Salesforce record, does it execute immediately - or propose the change for you to confirm first?
Option A - Safer: Propose and Confirm
Claude drafts the update and shows it to you: "I want to update Case #12345 - set Status to Closed, add this comment. Confirm?" You say yes, then it executes. Analogous to the written send-prohibition on Gmail-connected projects. Adds one step but gives you a review gate for every write. Recommended for V1.
Option B - Riskier: Direct Execute
Claude runs the update immediately when asked. Faster for high-volume support work. Risk: a misunderstanding or hallucinated field value goes directly into your production org with no review. No undo for most field updates. Not recommended until V1 has proven reliable.
Recommendation: Start with Option A (Propose and Confirm) for all object field updates. Knowledge Articles sit outside both options - they are read-only by standing rule, so there is no write to propose. Option B is appropriate only for Task creation and Case comment creation - additive actions that do not overwrite existing data. Upgrade specific operations to Option B after 60 days of clean operation if the volume warrants it.
Decision recorded: _________________________ (write your choice, date, and which operations are Option A vs. Option B)
Secondary Decision
For Flow and Security work: Claude proposes, human deploys. Always.
Flow deployments and security configuration changes must never be AI-executed regardless of which option you chose above. The risk is too high: a broken flow can fire incorrectly on thousands of records, and a wrong permission set change can grant or revoke access org-wide. Claude's role for flows and security is: read, explain, diagnose, write the fix. A human reviews and deploys in Setup or Workbench. This is not a setting - it is a hard rule to include in the Salesforce Admin Assistant's instructions.md.
4
Pre-Connection Decisions
Answer these before the connector is built - they define its shape
Decide Before Building
Authentication model
DECIDE Per-user OAuth vs. integration user (service account)
Per-user OAuth: Each staff member authenticates with their own Salesforce credentials. Claude operates within that person's existing Salesforce permission set. A support rep using Claude sees only what a support rep can see. Adam using Claude sees what an admin sees. This is the most secure model - least-privilege applies per session automatically.

Integration user / service account: One Salesforce user is created specifically for Claude. All sessions use it. Simpler to set up, but the integration user must be granted enough permissions to cover all use cases - which tends to mean broad access. If misconfigured, everyone's Claude session has admin-level visibility.

Recommendation: Per-user OAuth. More setup, correct security model. Use a Named Credential or OAuth Connected App in Salesforce configured per-user.
Decision: _________________________ (per-user OAuth / integration user + reason)
REQUIRED Create a dedicated Salesforce Connected App for Claude access - do not reuse existing app
Build a new Connected App in Salesforce specifically for Claude/Cowork integration. Do not reuse an existing Connected App (e.g., the one used for a reporting tool or another integration). A dedicated app means: you can revoke Claude's access independently of other integrations, you can see Claude-specific OAuth activity in Salesforce logs, and you can tune its scopes without affecting other tools.
In Salesforce Setup: App Manager → New Connected App. Name it clearly: "Claude AI - Cowork Integration." Configure OAuth scopes, IP restrictions, and refresh token policy before giving it to anyone.
OAuth scope - what permissions does the Connected App request?
REQUIRED Scope the Connected App to the minimum permissions needed
Do not use "Full access" (full) OAuth scope. Use the minimum scopes required for the use cases:

Recommended V1 scopes:
• api - access the REST API (required for all operations)
• refresh_token, offline_access - keep the session alive
• chatter_api - only if using Chatter for case comments

Do NOT include:
• full - too broad, grants everything
• web - unnecessary browser access
• visualforce - no VF pages needed
• custom_permissions - only if specifically needed
REQUIRED Define which Salesforce objects the connector can access - and list them explicitly
The connector's instructions.md must include an explicit allow-list of objects Claude can query and update. Objects not on the list are out of scope. V1 allow-list recommendation:

Read + write (with confirmation): Case, CaseComment, Task, Contact, Account
Read only, no exception: Knowledge Article. The permitted workflow is: Claude produces the article HTML in chat, and Adam copy-pastes it into the Knowledge article by hand. There is no direct write to Salesforce Knowledge, draft or otherwise.
Read only: Opportunity, Invoice/Subscription custom objects, Report, Dashboard, Flow (metadata), PermissionSet, Profile
Prohibited: Delete on any object, deploy Flow, modify PermissionSet or Profile
Approved object list recorded: _________________________
Who connects and when
DECIDE Which staff members connect their Salesforce in V1 - and in what order
Not everyone should connect at once. Recommended rollout: (1) Adam connects first - tests all use cases, validates the propose-before-execute model is working, confirms the object allow-list is correct. (2) After 2 weeks of clean operation, Tyler connects for support case use cases. (3) Kelsey and remaining staff connect after Tyler's use has been validated. Do not give everyone access on day one.
V1 rollout plan: _________________________ (who, in what order, with what timeline)
REQUIRED Maintain a connected-user log - who has authenticated and when
Keep a record of which Salesforce users have connected their credentials to Claude. Include: name, Salesforce username, date connected, Salesforce permission set/profile. This is your audit baseline. When someone leaves, you revoke the specific Connected App authorization for their account in Salesforce (Setup → Connected Apps OAuth Usage → revoke for that user).
Connected users: Adam Baker (____), Tyler Baughman (____), Kelsey Eberly (____)
5
Connected App Configuration in Salesforce
The Salesforce-side settings that control how Claude can connect
Admin Required
Connected App settings in Salesforce Setup
REQUIRED Set IP restrictions on the Connected App
In the Connected App settings, restrict which IP addresses can authenticate. Ideally, restrict to IP ranges used by Anthropic's Cowork infrastructure (check Anthropic documentation for egress IPs, or set to your office/VPN IP range as a minimum). This prevents the Connected App from being used by unauthorized parties even if credentials are compromised.
If Anthropic does not publish static egress IPs, use a VPN-based IP restriction so connections can only come from School Tech network locations.
REQUIRED Set token expiry and refresh policy
Configure the Connected App's refresh token policy: Refresh token expires after X hours of inactivity - do not set to "Refresh token is valid until revoked" (too long-lived). Recommended: 24-hour refresh token with 2-hour session token. This limits the window of exposure if a token is compromised without requiring frequent re-authentication for active users.
REQUIRED Restrict Connected App access to an approved user group or Permission Set
In the Connected App settings, set "Permitted Users" to "Admin approved users are pre-authorized." Create a Permission Set called "Claude AI Access" and assign it only to staff who are approved to use the Salesforce connector. Staff without this Permission Set cannot authenticate to the Connected App even if they know the credentials. This is your primary access gate.
Setup → App Manager → [Claude Connected App] → Manage → Edit Policies → Permitted Users: Admin approved. Then assign the Permission Set to approved users.
CONFIRM Enable and review Salesforce Event Monitoring for Connected App activity
If your Salesforce edition includes Event Monitoring (available in Enterprise and above), enable it for the Claude Connected App. This gives you a log of every API call Claude makes: which records were queried, which were updated, by which user, at what time. This is your audit trail. Even without full Event Monitoring, check Setup → Connected Apps OAuth Usage regularly to see active sessions.
CONFIRM Verify the audit trail - LastModifiedBy will show Claude's actions
When Claude updates a Salesforce record via a per-user OAuth connection, the record's LastModifiedBy will show the authenticated user's name (e.g., Tyler Baughman) - not "Claude" or a generic API user. This is correct behavior and means updates are attributable to specific people. Confirm this is true in your org by running a test update and checking the record history. Document it so support staff know their SF username is on record updates made via Claude.
6
Object-Level Access Checklist
Per-object guardrails to include in the Salesforce Admin Assistant's instructions.md
Highest Detail
The items below are instruction-level rules - what the Salesforce Admin Assistant's instructions.md must say about each object. These are not Salesforce permission settings; they are behavioral rules Claude follows during a session. Both layers are needed: Salesforce permissions set the ceiling, instructions set the actual behavior.
Cases and Case Comments
REQUIRED Field updates to Cases: propose before executing
Instructions must include: "Before updating any Case field (Status, Priority, Owner, Resolution), show the user the proposed change and ask for explicit confirmation: 'I want to update Case [number] - [field] from [current value] to [new value]. Confirm?' Do not execute the update until confirmed."
CONFIRM Case comments can be created directly (no confirmation required)
Adding a case comment is additive - it does not overwrite existing data. Claude can create case comments directly when asked without a confirmation step. This is the one Case write operation that does not need propose-before-execute. Verify this is acceptable for your workflow before enabling.
Opportunities and Financial Records
REQUIRED Opportunities: read-only in V1, no field updates
Instructions must include: "You have read access to Opportunity records. You may not update any Opportunity fields - including Amount, Close Date, Stage, or Probability. If asked to update an Opportunity, decline and explain that Opportunity updates require direct Salesforce access: 'I can read this Opportunity and help you think through the update, but I cannot modify Opportunity records directly.'"
REQUIRED Invoice and subscription data: read-only, never modify
Financial records (invoices, subscription terms, billing amounts) are read-only for Claude. Instructions must prohibit any update to financial fields. Include: "You may look up invoice numbers, subscription status, and billing terms to answer questions. You may not modify, create, or delete invoice or subscription records under any circumstances."
Knowledge Articles
REQUIRED Knowledge Articles: READ ONLY - no direct write of any kind, including drafts
Instructions must include: "You may NOT create, edit or publish a Salesforce Knowledge Article, and that includes drafts. Read Knowledge content freely. To change an article, produce the article HTML in chat and hand it to Adam." The permitted workflow is: Claude produces the article HTML in chat, and Adam copy-pastes it into the Knowledge article by hand. There is no direct write to Salesforce Knowledge, draft or otherwise. This supersedes the earlier draft-write allowance on this page, which conflicted with the standing never-write-to-Salesforce-Knowledge rule. Ruled 2026-08-20: the standing rule wins.
Flows and Automation
REQUIRED Flows: read and propose fixes only - never deploy
Instructions must include: "You can read Flow definitions, explain their logic, identify likely errors, and write corrected Flow XML or outline the changes needed. You may not deploy, activate, or deactivate a Flow directly. For any Flow change, provide the fix as text and instruct the user to apply it in Setup or Workbench after reviewing. Never attempt to deploy a Flow via API."
Security and Permissions
REQUIRED Security config: read for audit only - never modify permission sets or profiles
Instructions must include: "You can read and describe Permission Sets, Profiles, Field-Level Security settings, Sharing Rules, and Organization-Wide Defaults for audit and diagnostic purposes. You may not modify, create, or delete any security configuration. For any security fix, describe what change is needed and where to make it in Setup - do not attempt the change via API."
ADMIN ONLY Security and flow work is restricted to Adam's sessions
Flow debugging, security auditing, and admin configuration assistance are use cases for Adam only. The Salesforce Admin Assistant instructions.md should include a role-detection rule: "If the user asks for help with Flows, Permission Sets, Profiles, Sharing Rules, or other admin configuration topics and they are not the system administrator (Adam Baker), respond: 'Admin configuration questions are routed to Adam. Please contact him directly with this request.'"
Delete operations
REQUIRED Delete is prohibited for all objects in all sessions
Instructions must include: "You may not delete any Salesforce record under any circumstances, for any user, for any stated reason. If asked to delete a record, decline: 'Record deletion is not something I can do. If a record needs to be deleted, that must be done directly in Salesforce by an admin after confirming it is appropriate.' This rule has no exceptions."
7
Staff Rules by Role
Different staff use Salesforce differently - rules and training vary accordingly
Support team (Tyler, Kelsey) - primary use: cases, case comments, KA lookup
Support staff understand what Claude can and cannot update in Cases
Before first use: walk each support team member through the propose-before-execute flow for Case field updates. They need to know: (1) Claude will show them a proposed update and ask for confirmation before executing it. (2) Case comments can be added directly. (3) They should never ask Claude to close, reassign, or reprioritize a case without reviewing Claude's proposed change first. (4) If Claude's proposed update looks wrong, say so - do not confirm an update that doesn't match what you intended.
Support staff are told not to use Claude for Opportunities or financial records. That is guidance, not a capability limit
Support staff occasionally look up contract status or subscription details for context. They should know: Claude is instructed not to update an Opportunity or Invoice record. It is not prevented from doing so: the live sf CLI path runs with full write against production, so this is a written rule and nothing else. If they need to modify contract terms or financial records, they do that directly in Salesforce.
Adam (admin) - primary use: flows, security, admin questions, all objects
ADMIN ONLY Adam reviews all Claude-proposed Flow and security changes before applying them
Even for Adam, the rule is propose-then-deploy for Flow and security work. Claude provides the fix in text; Adam reads it, agrees with it, and applies it in Setup or Workbench. This extra review step is justified: a wrong flow change or security misconfiguration can affect all org users and data. Claude's role is to be the expert diagnostician and drafter - not the one who pulls the trigger.
ADMIN ONLY Adam does not share Claude's Salesforce output with external parties without review
Security audit output (e.g., "here are all users with Modify All Data permission") or flow logic extracted by Claude is sensitive internal information. Do not paste Claude's Salesforce security analysis into external communications, shared docs, or ticket threads visible to customers or vendors without reviewing and redacting first.
All staff - shared rules
Every staff member using Claude+Salesforce knows: their SF username is on every update Claude makes
Because Claude uses per-user OAuth, every record update appears in Salesforce as modified by that person. Staff need to understand this means they are accountable for updates Claude makes in their session. Reviewing Claude's proposed changes before confirming is not optional - it is their sign-off on that change appearing under their name in the audit trail.
Staff know what to do if Claude proposes an incorrect Salesforce update
If Claude proposes an update that looks wrong: (1) Do not confirm it. (2) Correct Claude in the conversation: "That's wrong - the status should be [X] not [Y]." (3) Claude will show a revised proposal. (4) If Claude keeps getting it wrong on a specific type of update, log it via the Agent Quality Logger and notify Adam. This is the feedback loop that improves the tool.
8
Ongoing Monitoring and Audit
After the connector is live - what to check and when
Periodic checks
Weekly (first month): Review Salesforce record history for unexpected Claude-assisted changes
For the first four weeks after go-live, run a weekly check: in Salesforce, pull a report of all records modified in the past 7 days by any of the Claude-connected users. Spot-check 5-10 records. Look for unexpected field changes, fields set to blank, or records in an unusual state. This catches systematic errors early before they compound.
Monthly: Review Connected App OAuth Usage in Salesforce Setup
Setup → Connected Apps OAuth Usage. Review: (1) Which users have active tokens for the Claude Connected App. (2) Are all of them current staff? If a former staff member shows an active token, revoke immediately. (3) Are any unexpected users listed? Investigate. (4) Token count per user - if one user has an unusually high number of active tokens, that may indicate a misconfiguration.
Quarterly: Re-evaluate object access permissions - is the allow-list still appropriate?
As the Salesforce Admin Assistant matures, the object allow-list may need to expand (e.g., adding Opportunity write access after 60 days) or contract (if an object is causing problems). Review quarterly: what is Claude actually being used for in Salesforce? Does the current allow-list match real usage? Is there anything on the allow-list that has never been used and could be trimmed?
When any staff member leaves: revoke their Connected App authorization immediately
Offboarding step (add to User Management Guide): Setup → Connected Apps OAuth Usage → find the departing user → Revoke. Also remove them from the "Claude AI Access" Permission Set. Do this the same day as their departure - do not wait for a quarterly audit. An active token for a former employee is a live security exposure.
This step does not exist yet. Verified 2026-08-20: the User Management Guide's offboarding procedure has five steps and none of them revokes a Salesforce credential or a Google OAuth grant. The Google Access Security Checklist correctly asks for the step to be ADDED; this page previously said it was already there, which is how the gap survived. Treat it as outstanding.
9
Incident Response
What to do if Claude updates something it shouldn't have
Know Before It Happens
Claude updated a Salesforce record incorrectly (wrong field value, wrong record)
Step 1: Check the record's Field History or Audit Trail to confirm exactly what changed and when. Step 2: Manually correct the field in Salesforce. Step 3: If the incorrect value triggered any automation (flow, workflow rule, process builder), check whether downstream records were also affected. Step 4: Log the incident via the Agent Quality Logger - describe what was asked, what Claude did, and what the correct action should have been. Step 5: Adam reviews and updates the Salesforce Admin Assistant instructions to prevent the same error.
Claude queried or returned data from an object it should not have accessed
Step 1: Identify which record(s) were returned and whether the data is sensitive. Step 2: Check the Salesforce Admin Assistant instructions.md - is the object on the allow-list? If yes, the instruction is wrong. If no, the connector may be ignoring the instruction. Step 3: If data was displayed to the user and retained in a conversation log, note this. Step 4: Log via Agent Quality Logger. Step 5: Adam tightens the instructions and/or revises the Connected App's permission scope to add a platform-level restriction for that object.
Claude executed a change without the confirm step (bypassed propose-before-execute)
This is a critical instructions failure. Step 1: Check what changed and reverse it if possible. Step 2: Immediately suspend the Salesforce Admin Assistant for all users until the instructions are fixed. Step 3: Review the full conversation to understand how the confirm step was bypassed - was the user inadvertently phrasing a request as a direct command? Did Claude misinterpret? Step 4: Rewrite the relevant instruction with a stronger, more explicit confirm requirement. Step 5: Test the fix with a controlled update before resuming use.
Do not resume until you can demonstrate the propose-before-execute rule is reliably enforced across 3 consecutive test sessions.
Suspected unauthorized access - Connected App token may be compromised
Step 1: Immediately revoke all active tokens for the Claude Connected App (Setup → Connected Apps OAuth Usage → Revoke All). Step 2: Review Salesforce Login History and Event Monitoring for any unusual API activity in the last 30 days. Step 3: Reset the Connected App's OAuth credentials (Consumer Key and Secret). Step 4: Re-issue access to approved staff only after confirming the source of the compromise. Step 5: Review whether the compromised token was used to access any sensitive objects (Opportunities, financial records, security config) and assess whether further action is needed.
